nodes.details: The vulnerability is accessible through web endpoints that perform form validation and return status messages directly to the client.
The server processes user input and generates validation error responses that are transmitted to the client without content filtering.
The validation logic fails to neutralize or escape HTML characters within error messages, enabling the injection of arbitrary markup.
The remediation updates the validation routine to explicitly remove HTML tags from error messages prior to returning them to the interface.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-site Scripting)

nodes.details: These methods process incoming form validation requests and interact with session attributes, serving as the direct attack surface for the vulnerability.
The application fails to sanitize or escape error messages generated during form validation before rendering them in the HTTP response.
User-controllable data or internal state triggers error responses that are directly embedded into HTML without proper escaping, enabling injection attacks.
The patch adds POST request annotations to restrict endpoint access, and the vulnerability description confirms HTML tags are stripped from error messages to prevent injection.
The vulnerability affects Jenkins Stapler methods used for form validation and data population in the plugin.
The plugin processes form validation requests without sanitizing the resulting error messages before returning them to the client.
Error messages generated during form validation are not escaped, allowing raw HTML to be injected into the response.
The patch updates method signatures to enforce POST requests and item context validation, aligning with the security update that strips HTML tags from error messages.

Error messages containing untrusted data are directly rendered in the response without proper neutralization, allowing HTML injection.
The patch ensures HTML tags are removed from error messages before they are returned to the client.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

nodes.details: Multiple descriptor methods handling form data and validation serve as the attack surface for the vulnerability.
The plugin fails to sanitize error messages returned by form validation methods before rendering them in the UI.
Error messages are directly exposed to the client without neutralizing HTML characters, allowing injection of malicious markup.
The patch modifies descriptor methods to require POST requests and pass item context, while the underlying fix removes HTML tags from error messages to prevent injection.

nodes.details: The vulnerability is triggered when the printer component processes string objects for formatting.
The method splits input strings by newline characters without enforcing a size limit on the resulting array.
Creating an unbounded array from string splitting consumes excessive memory, causing an out-of-memory exception.
The patch restricts the split operation using a maximum row count and throws an exception upon truncation to prevent resource exhaustion.
The vulnerability is triggered when the database server is launched via the command-line interface using the main entry method.
A local user or attacker must supply the web admin password flag with a cleartext value during command-line execution.
The argument parser incorrectly accepts the password flag from the command line, causing the cleartext value to be exposed in the system process list.
The patch adds a command-line detection flag to reject the password argument during CLI execution, forcing configuration via files instead.
The vulnerability is triggered when the database server is launched via command-line arguments that specify the web administration password.
An attacker requires local system access to inspect running processes and extract command-line arguments.
The command-line interface accepts unencrypted passwords, making them visible in the operating system's process listing.
The update introduces password encoding and length checks to prevent cleartext passwords from being passed via command-line arguments.
The vulnerability is triggered when the web admin console is initialized via command-line arguments containing a password parameter.
The application accepts password values directly from process arguments, making them visible to local users through standard process listing tools.
The original method processed arbitrary password strings without strict format validation, allowing cleartext or improperly encoded inputs to be stored.
The update removes automatic hashing logic and strictly requires a 128-character input, throwing an exception for any other length to prevent arbitrary password assignment.
The routine functions as a form validation handler that tests external service connectivity.
The validation handler executed without verifying user privileges, permitting low-privilege users to trigger it.
The absence of permission verification and HTTP method restrictions allowed unauthorized credential retrieval and cross-site request forgery.
The update introduces explicit privilege verification and mandates POST requests to restrict access to authorized administrators or job configurators.
This method serves as the initial configuration point where users can modify SAX parser features, triggering the vulnerability.
The vulnerability requires an attacker to invoke the feature configuration method to alter parser behavior regarding external resources.
The configuration method stored the external entity flag without updating the corresponding entity expansion setting, allowing uncontrolled external entity processing.
The patch introduces a conditional check to automatically update the entity expansion state whenever the external entity feature is modified.

nodes.details: The routine constructs output file paths by concatenating user-supplied application name and version parameters without validation.
The system accepts application name and version parameters from Pipeline steps, which are directly incorporated into file paths.
The filename generation logic fails to sanitize user-controlled parameters, allowing path traversal sequences to be embedded in the resulting path.
The patch introduces a sanitization step using an encoding utility to neutralize special characters in the constructed filename before returning it.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

nodes.details: The endpoint processes HTTP requests to retrieve and serve file attachments based on user-provided parameters.
The application directly incorporates an unsanitized request parameter into the file system path construction logic.
Directly using the unvalidated parameter to build the file path enables attackers to traverse directories and access arbitrary system files.
The patch introduces a validation step to sanitize the user-supplied parameter before it is used to construct the target file path.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

nodes.details: The vulnerability is triggered when the plugin executes file reading operations through the Jenkins agent process.
The vulnerability is only exploitable on Jenkins versions 2.318 and earlier, or LTS 2.303.2 and earlier, where agent processes can execute arbitrary file reads.
The plugin uses remote execution mechanisms to run file reading operations on the Jenkins controller from an agent process, bypassing security restrictions.
The fix removes the remote execution wrapper and replaces it with a direct local file read to prevent execution on agent processes.
The vulnerability is triggered through the service handling user logical deletion and restoration operations.
The service methods accept a list of user identifiers from external requests without prior validation.
The implementation manually formatted the identifier list into a string and passed it directly to the data mapper, enabling malicious input to manipulate the underlying SQL query.
The patch removes manual string formatting and passes the identifier list directly to the mapper, ensuring safe parameterized query execution.
The vulnerability is triggered through a plugin message that allows an agent to initiate actions on the Jenkins controller.
An attacker must compromise a Jenkins agent process to send malicious requests that trigger the insecure functionality.
The plugin incorrectly implements an agent-to-controller message that creates user-specified directories and parses files without sufficient validation.
The update changes the message type from agent-to-controller to controller-to-agent, preventing unauthorized execution and file operations on the controller.
The annotation method processes test report text and automatically converts detected web addresses into interactive hyperlinks.
An attacker requires Item or Configure permission to inject malicious content into the test report output.
The implementation wraps matched URLs in anchor tags without validating the link content, allowing malicious scripts to be embedded and executed in the browser.
The patch removes the regular expression replacement that converts URLs to clickable links, thereby eliminating the vector for stored cross-site scripting.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

nodes.details: The vulnerability occurs during the processing of JUnit test report output where HTTP(S) URLs are identified and transformed into HTML elements.
Attackers possessing Item/Configure permission can inject arbitrary HTTP(S) URLs into stored JUnit test reports, which are subsequently processed by the plugin.
The plugin converts detected HTTP(S) URLs into clickable HTML anchor tags without adequate sanitization, enabling stored cross-site scripting when the output is rendered.
The patch updates test expectations to verify that URLs are returned as plain text instead of being wrapped in HTML anchor tags, removing the unsafe conversion logic.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-site Scripting)

nodes.details: This execution point processes user-provided parameters for the input step and initiates the archiving process on the Jenkins controller.
The vulnerability requires a pipeline author to configure a file parameter within an input step, which activates the underlying file handling logic.
The system archives uploaded files using the parameter name directly as a relative path without sanitization, allowing arbitrary file creation or overwriting on the controller.
The patch adds validation checks to detect file parameters and aborts execution or issues warnings, effectively prohibiting their use to prevent filesystem manipulation.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

nodes.details: These methods construct file system paths from user-supplied container and key parameters without prior validation.
Authenticated clients can supply arbitrary blob keys that are directly resolved against the storage root directory.
The implementation fails to sanitize or verify user-controlled path components, allowing directory traversal sequences to escape the intended container scope.
The update introduces path normalization and a validation routine to ensure all resolved file paths remain strictly within the designated container directory.

nodes.details: The method dynamically assembles SQL query fragments using multiple user-supplied parameters to filter data.
External inputs including search terms, analysis identifiers, time windows, and domain values are accepted without prior validation.
Raw input values are directly interpolated into SQL statement strings using format functions, allowing malicious characters to break out of string literals.
The update introduces SQL escaping utilities for string parameters and enforces strict integer parsing for identifier arrays to neutralize injection vectors.

nodes.details: The deletion method processes user-submitted bundle names to remove files from the controller without validating the input paths or checking required permissions.
The HTTP request allows attackers to supply arbitrary file paths via a JSON parameter that are directly concatenated to the root directory.
The implementation fails to verify that submitted paths correspond to legitimate support bundles or that the requester holds the required download permission.
The update restricts deletion to only pre-existing valid bundles and ensures access control is enforced before processing the request.

nodes.details: The handler processes file modifications for change requests, serving as the entry point for editing wiki documents.
Users with change request and view rights can edit any page by default, including those containing sensitive password fields.
The system fails to restrict editing of documents containing password fields, allowing attackers to extract password hashes via exported XML.
The patch introduces a rights verification step to deny editing access for documents containing password fields, throwing an exception when unauthorized.
This method serves as the primary execution path for initializing and preparing documents within the change request workflow, directly handling user edit requests.
The system grants change request editing capabilities by default to users possessing view access, enabling document modifications and subsequent XML export without explicit restrictions.
The document preparation logic proceeded without verifying whether the current user had explicit permission to modify the target document via a change request, allowing unauthorized edits.
The patch introduces an explicit authorization check to verify user permissions before allowing document preparation, blocking unauthorized edits through the change request mechanism.
The handler processes incoming requests to create change requests, serving as the initial point where document editing permissions are evaluated.
The system grants change request editing rights by default, allowing users with view access to target pages to initiate edits without additional restrictions.
The handler fails to verify whether a user is authorized to edit a document containing sensitive data before allowing the change request to proceed.
The patch introduces a rights manager check to deny editing permissions for documents containing password fields, throwing an exception if the user lacks authorization.
The vulnerability is triggered during the LDAP connection setup process within the Active Directory authentication plugin.
The issue only manifests when the Jenkins instance is configured to utilize StartTLS for secure LDAP communication.
TLS configuration parameters were not properly propagated to individual domain objects, resulting in inadequate certificate validation during server binding.
The update modifies the binding logic to explicitly pass TLS configuration and iteratively assigns it to each domain during object restoration.
The vulnerability is triggered when the plugin establishes an LDAP connection for user authentication or group lookup, specifically during the bind operation.
The vulnerability requires the Jenkins Active Directory plugin to be configured to use StartTLS for securing LDAP connections.
The plugin failed to properly propagate or apply the domain-specific TLS configuration during LDAP bind operations, leading to improper certificate validation.
The patch removes the class-level TLS configuration field and updates all LDAP bind calls to explicitly use the domain-specific TLS configuration to ensure proper certificate validation.
The vulnerability is triggered during the initialization and configuration resolution of Active Directory security realms.
The issue manifests when Jenkins is configured to use StartTLS for connecting to Active Directory servers.
The plugin lacks proper validation logic for TLS certificates across configured domains, enabling server impersonation attacks.
The update ensures TLS configuration is correctly resolved per domain, preserving null values when not persisted to disk.
The vulnerability is triggered during the StartTLS connection process when Jenkins attempts to authenticate with an Active Directory server.
The vulnerability requires Jenkins to be configured to use StartTLS for connecting to the Active Directory server.
The plugin fails to properly validate the server's certificate during the StartTLS handshake, allowing attackers to impersonate the target server.
The patch refactors test initialization into a dynamic setup method and updates domain validation calls to include an additional parameter, ensuring tests align with updated security configurations.
Processes user-supplied server addresses and security parameters during domain configuration testing.
Requires the application to be configured to utilize StartTLS for establishing secure directory service connections.
The underlying connection logic omits proper verification of the remote server's TLS certificate, enabling server impersonation.
Introduces a dedicated TLS configuration parameter to mandate certificate validation during connection and authentication binding.
The vulnerability is triggered when the form validation method processes user-supplied input and returns an HTML response.
The endpoint accepts a user-controlled parameter that is directly used in the response without prior validation or sanitization.
User input is concatenated directly into an HTML markup string without applying XML escaping, enabling script injection.
The patch modifies the response generation to apply XML escaping to the user parameter before embedding it in the HTML output.

Versions prior to 2.5.2 parse XML files without restricting external document type definitions or entity references.
The default transformer factory configuration permits downloading external DTDs and expanding entity references during transformation.
The patch replaces direct factory instantiation with a helper method that enforces disabled external DTD processing by default.

The XML parser is invoked without explicit restrictions on external document type definitions or entity expansion.
The absence of a configured external resource policy allows the parser to fetch and process arbitrary external entities.

The patch replaces direct factory instantiation with a helper method to enforce secure defaults and disable external DTD processing by default.

The underlying SAX parser and document builder lacked configuration to restrict access to external schemas and DTDs, allowing external entity expansion.

The XML processing configuration fails to restrict external entity resolution and DTD processing by default, allowing potential data exfiltration and resource access.
The patch delegates transformer creation to a helper method and directly configures output properties to standardize XML processing and enforce restricted external access.

The patch replaces direct parser instantiation with a utility method that enforces restricted XML processing and disables external DTD handling.

Versions prior to the fix automatically download and expand external document type definitions and entity references during XML parsing without user restriction.
The XML parser lacks built-in safeguards to disable external DTD processing, enabling potential data exfiltration and resource access through malicious entity injection.
The update replaces manual test logic with parameterized calls to introduce configurable processing modes, allowing users to explicitly prohibit or ignore external DTDs and entities.

nodes.details: This method handles the initialization and management of temporary files used during recording operations.
The execution environment enforces security policies that restrict direct file system access, necessitating explicit privilege elevation for file operations.
The file creation process lacks proper privilege handling, making it susceptible to race conditions and potential unauthorized file manipulation.
The patch wraps the file management logic within a privileged action block to bypass security restrictions and ensure secure file operations.
The vulnerability is triggered when the server processes client-supplied terminal dimension data via the Telnet negotiation protocol.
An attacker must establish an unauthenticated connection to the Telnet server and successfully negotiate the window size option to inject arbitrary values.
The input validation logic only enforces a minimum threshold for terminal dimensions, allowing excessively large values to bypass checks and trigger expensive rendering operations.
The update introduces upper bound checks alongside existing lower bound validations, ensuring that out-of-range terminal dimensions are clamped to safe default values.
Initializes processing parameters for JSON document handling.
Processing JSON documents with excessive nesting depth triggers the issue.
Lack of a configurable maximum depth limit permits unbounded recursion, causing stack overflow during document processing.
The patch adds initialization for a configurable maximum depth limit to restrict nesting levels.

An attacker supplies a JSON document with an excessively large depth of nested objects or arrays.
The parser fails to enforce a maximum depth limit when tracking nested contexts, causing uncontrolled memory allocation.
The patch initializes the internal tracking stack with a configurable limit and aborts processing when the nesting depth exceeds this threshold.
This component processes the target URL following successful user authentication, determining where the user should be redirected.
The handler retrieves a target URL from session attributes or request parameters without verifying its origin or destination.
The original logic directly returns the resolved URL after context path adjustment, permitting arbitrary external domains for redirection.
The update introduces a safety verification step that checks the target URL before redirection, defaulting to a safe internal URL if validation fails.
The test case validates the behavior of the API key name accessor method during object initialization.
Prior to the patch, the API key name attribute returned the exact same value as the secret key, allowing full credential exposure.
The implementation failed to apply any masking logic to the name attribute, causing it to mirror the sensitive key value directly.
The update modifies the expected output to ensure the name attribute returns a truncated and masked string instead of the full secret.
The method serves as the direct access point for retrieving the API key, exposing sensitive credentials to callers.
The method returns the complete API key without restriction, creating a condition where sensitive credentials are fully accessible.
The implementation fails to obscure the API key during retrieval, allowing unauthorized parties to obtain the full credential and bypass access filters.
The patch modifies the return value to truncate and replace the middle characters with asterisks, preventing full credential exposure.
The application starts an embedded HTTP server that configures connectors and request handlers to process incoming traffic.
The vulnerability requires the system to rely on class pattern matching mechanisms for defining access control or filtering rules.
The original implementation used an incorrect API method for defining system class patterns, resulting in improper evaluation of access control rules and enabling unauthorized URL access.
The patch replaces the outdated pattern method with the appropriate class matcher API to ensure accurate evaluation of access control rules and prevent filter bypass.
The method exposes an HTTP interface for testing Active Directory connectivity and user authentication, processing provided credentials.
The endpoint previously accepted HTTP GET requests, enabling external parties to trigger the authentication test functionality without user consent.
The absence of a POST requirement permits cross-site request forgery, allowing attackers to initiate connection tests with arbitrary credentials.
The patch introduces a POST requirement annotation to restrict the endpoint, preventing unauthorized cross-site request forgery attempts.
This HTTP endpoint performs Active Directory connection and authentication configuration tests.
The endpoint previously accepted GET requests, allowing external sites to trigger sensitive validation operations without user consent.
The absence of a POST requirement enabled attackers to forge requests that execute connection tests with specified credentials.
The patch applies a POST-only annotation to the validation method, preventing cross-site request forgery attacks.

nodes.details: Serves as the primary routine for deriving native memory addresses during cryptographic nonce generation.
Triggers when JVM security policies disable Unsafe access, preventing standard direct buffer address resolution.
Incorrect memory address resolution for pooled buffers leads to out-of-bounds reads during cryptographic operations.
Switches to a reader-relative address method to ensure correct native pointer resolution for direct buffers.
The execute method derives native memory addresses for ByteBufs to pass to BoringSSL for cryptographic operations.
The vulnerability requires a JVM configuration where Unsafe access is restricted or unavailable, causing direct ByteBufs to lack exposed memory addresses.
Manual calculation of native buffer addresses fails to account for pooled buffer boundaries, allowing access to adjacent memory regions during cryptographic operations.
The patch replaces manual pointer arithmetic with dedicated memory address retrieval methods to ensure correct buffer boundaries are respected.
The function derives native memory addresses for cryptographic operations, serving as the entry point for the vulnerability when unsafe access is disabled.
The vulnerability requires a JVM configuration where unsafe memory access is restricted, causing the buffer allocator to return instances that do not expose their memory addresses.

The original implementation fails to account for the buffer's reader index and readable bytes, returning the address of the entire buffer instead of the active readable portion, leading to out-of-bounds reads and memory corruption.
The patch updates the memory address derivation to explicitly incorporate the buffer's reader index and readable bytes, ensuring only the valid readable portion is accessed.
Handles parsing and transformation of inline macros within the rendering context.
Occurs when the parser processes nested macros inside a restricted transformation context, such as within comments.
The parser fails to preserve the restricted attribute of the transformation context during nested macro execution.
The patch introduces a verification step to ensure the transformation context remains unrestricted when passed to the rendering context.
The vulnerability originates in the macro content parsing logic where transformation contexts are instantiated for nested macro execution.
The issue occurs when executing nested macros within a restricted transformation context, requiring the parser to propagate security constraints to child contexts.
The parser fails to retrieve and pass the restricted attribute from the parent transformation context to newly created child transformation contexts during parsing.
The patch retrieves the parent transformation context, checks its restricted status, and explicitly passes this boolean flag to the newly instantiated transformation context.
The vulnerability occurs during the authentication success callback when processing the RelayState parameter from the SAML assertion.
The system accepts an external RelayState value from the SAML response and directly incorporates it into a client-side redirection script.
The original implementation applied HTML escaping to the RelayState, which fails to properly sanitize the value for safe embedding within a JavaScript string context.
The patch replaces the previous escaping mechanism with UTF-8 URL encoding to ensure the RelayState is safely encoded before script generation.
The authentication flow processes the RelayState parameter from SAML responses and embeds it into client-side navigation logic.
The application accepts user-supplied RelayState values and directly incorporates them into HTML or JavaScript contexts without adequate sanitization.
The handler applies HTML entity encoding to the RelayState value, which is insufficient for preventing script execution when the value is interpreted in a URL fragment or script context.
The patch replaces HTML entity encoding with percent-encoding for special characters in the RelayState, ensuring safe handling in URL fragments and preventing cross-site scripting.

The patch introduces an explicit permission verification step to restrict endpoint access exclusively to administrators.

Jenkins automatically processes escape sequences in environment variables, interpreting double dollar signs as a single dollar sign before passing them to the build process.
The plugin directly inserts unescaped secret values into the build environment map, allowing Jenkins' variable resolver to modify the original secret strings.
The patch modifies the environment population logic to iterate through secret values and escape dollar signs by doubling them, preventing unintended variable resolution.

Multiple exposed endpoints allow retrieval of Jenkins credential information without proper access control.
The vulnerability requires the attacker to possess at least Overall or Read permission on the Jenkins instance.
The affected endpoints lack mandatory permission verification and do not enforce POST request methods, enabling unauthorized access and CSRF attacks.
The patch adds the @POST annotation to mandate POST requests and introduces context parameters to enable proper permission validation.
Accepts user-supplied URL parameters for on-the-fly validation without requiring POST.
The endpoint is accessible to users with Overall or Read permissions and processes GET requests.
The application directly opens and fetches content from a user-supplied URL without validating the target or restricting the HTTP method.
The patch adds a RequirePOST annotation to restrict the endpoint to POST requests, mitigating GET-based SSRF and CSRF attacks.
The method handles on-the-fly URL validation for repository configuration without enforcing HTTP method restrictions.
Attackers possessing Overall or Read permissions can invoke the validation function to trigger external network requests.
The endpoint accepts user-supplied URLs and executes HTTP GET requests to them without validating the request method or restricting internal access.
The patch introduces a RequirePOST annotation to restrict the endpoint to POST requests, mitigating the ability to trigger GET-based SSRF.
The method serves as a user-facing validation routine that processes external URLs provided by the requester.
Exploitation requires only Overall or Read access, as the original implementation did not restrict request methods or enforce stricter authentication.
The endpoint directly constructs and executes HTTP GET requests to user-supplied addresses without verifying the request method or destination legitimacy.
The patch introduces a RequirePOST annotation to mandate POST requests, thereby preventing unauthorized GET-based server-side request forgery.
This method serves as a user-facing form validation handler that processes an externally provided URL parameter to verify repository accessibility.
The vulnerability requires only Overall or Read permissions, allowing low-privilege users to trigger the endpoint and initiate outbound network requests.
The handler accepts a user-supplied URL and directly opens an HTTP connection to it without restricting the request method or validating the target, enabling SSRF.
The patch introduces a method restriction annotation to ensure the endpoint only accepts POST requests, preventing the vulnerable GET-based SSRF vector.
Exposes a web function that processes user-supplied URLs to verify repository connectivity.
Attackers possessing only read permissions can trigger the validation logic without administrative oversight.
The function directly constructs a network connection from user input without validating the target host or protocol.
The patch enforces a POST request requirement to prevent automated or cross-site GET requests from triggering the outbound connection.
The method serves as a form validation handler that processes user-supplied URLs to verify repository configurations.
The vulnerability can be triggered by attackers possessing only Overall or Read permissions, as the endpoint lacks sufficient access restrictions.
The application directly constructs and opens a network connection to a user-controlled URL without validating the target host, enabling SSRF.
The patch introduces a RequirePOST annotation to the validation method, ensuring that only POST requests can trigger the URL verification logic.
The vulnerability occurs during the extraction of zip archive contents to a specified destination directory.
The application processes externally provided zip files containing arbitrary entry names without prior sanitization.
The original implementation relied on a basic canonical path prefix check that failed to properly normalize paths, allowing directory traversal sequences to bypass the restriction.
The patch replaces the manual canonical path check with a dedicated validation function to ensure extracted files remain within the target directory before any file operations.

nodes.details: The vulnerability is triggered during the extraction of zip archives via the extraction routine of the Unzip utility class.
An attacker supplies a crafted archive containing entries with relative path traversal sequences to exploit the extraction process.
The extraction implementation lacks proper path normalization and validation, permitting directory traversal attacks during file extraction.
The update modifies the validation mechanism to explicitly detect and block file write operations that attempt to escape the designated output directory.

nodes.details: This method serves as the primary entry point for processing the vulnerable configuration property that previously handled serialized data.
Prior to version 0.12.0, the configuration property stored data as a hex-encoded serialized Java object that could be externally modified.
The application directly deserialized externally controlled serialized objects and JNDI references, enabling remote code execution through malicious factory class locations.
The patch updates the method signature to declare a CSV parsing exception, indicating a transition to a safe CSV-based format that validates input during parsing.
This property acts as a writable configuration point that processes external input to reconstruct a map of user overrides.
The vulnerability requires the application to expose the userOverridesAsString property, allowing external input to be processed as a hex-encoded serialized object.
The original implementation directly deserialized untrusted hex-encoded byte arrays without validation, enabling arbitrary class instantiation and remote code execution via embedded JNDI references.
The patch eliminates Java object deserialization by converting the property format to a safe CSV structure that parses strings and key-value pairs without instantiating arbitrary classes.
The vulnerability is triggered during the stream processing phase when parsing chunk headers and allocating buffers for decompression.
An attacker must supply a maliciously crafted compressed stream containing an excessively large chunk size value in the header.
The implementation only verifies that the chunk size is non-negative but lacks validation against a maximum allowable limit, leading to unbounded heap allocation.
The patch adds a validation step to reject any chunk size exceeding a predefined maximum threshold before buffer allocation occurs.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

nodes.details: The vulnerability is triggered during the deserialization of untyped JSON objects and arrays.
The deserialization process accepts JSON input containing arbitrarily nested structures without enforcing a maximum nesting limit.
Recursive processing of nested JSON fields and arrays lacks depth tracking, leading to stack overflow and denial of service.
The patch introduces a depth parameter to track recursion levels and throws an exception when nesting exceeds a predefined threshold.
The constructor initializes the deserialization stream, serving as the primary entry point for processing serialized objects from disk.
Attackers must be able to control the serialized Java objects stored on disk that the plugin attempts to deserialize.
The deserialization stream is initialized without applying JEP-200 protections, allowing arbitrary class instantiation during object reconstruction.
The patch updates the superclass initialization to explicitly pass a classloader and a default class filter, restricting deserialization to safe types.
The vulnerability is triggered through the security service integration library, allowing unauthenticated actors to bypass access controls.
An attacker must interact with the library's security token processing mechanisms without prior authentication to exploit the flaw.
The library fails to properly validate permissions during token processing, enabling privilege escalation under specific conditions.
The issue is resolved by upgrading to version 2.17.0 or 3.3.0, which implements proper authorization checks to prevent arbitrary permission assignment.
The system utilizes OAuth2 service configuration to perform token validation and enforce security policies.
Static or misconfigured domain settings create conditions where authentication checks can be bypassed.
The validation mechanism fails to properly restrict permissions, allowing unauthenticated users to escalate privileges.
The patch modifies the configuration builder to use dynamic service endpoints instead of static defaults.
The test suite validates instance caching and default validator composition for the JWT validation builder, which serves as the primary entry point for token authentication.
The vulnerability manifests when the builder initializes its default set of validators, potentially allowing improper privilege escalation if validation steps are misconfigured.
The builder incorrectly configured its default validators, resulting in insufficient validation checks that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to obtain arbitrary permissions.
The patch modifies the expected validator count and removes a specific validator type from the default configuration, aligning the test assertions with the corrected behavior.
The vulnerability resides in the XSUAA JWT signature validator component responsible for verifying token authenticity and enforcing access policies.
The validator relies on external service configurations and token key services to perform authentication checks, creating a potential bypass vector.
Inadequate validation logic allows unauthenticated requests to bypass security controls, leading to privilege escalation and unauthorized permission assignment.

nodes.summary: correct configuration and key retrieval logic
nodes.details: The patch updates configuration property handling and token key retrieval mechanisms to ensure the validator properly enforces authentication requirements.
The vulnerability is triggered during the decoding and validation phase of JSON Web Tokens.
An unauthenticated attacker must inject a maliciously crafted JWKS URL into the JWT header.
The library fails to properly validate the JWKS URL, allowing attackers to redirect token key requests and escalate privileges.
The patch enforces rigorous validation of the JWKS URL source before token decoding to prevent unauthorized access.
The method configures mock OAuth services and application servers prior to test execution.
The vulnerability manifests when the application server initialization flag is enabled during test configuration.
The application server was initialized before the mock OAuth server, and server options were not validated, causing incorrect endpoint routing and privilege escalation.
The patch reorders component startup to initialize the mock server first and adds a conditional check to properly configure server options before starting the application server.
The vulnerability is triggered during the JWT decoding process in the XsuaaJwtDecoder component. It occurs when verification keys or domain information are missing or malformed.

The vulnerability requires specific conditions where the JWT header lacks valid verification keys, JWKS URLs, or UAA domain information. This allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass authentication checks.
Inadequate validation of JWT verification keys and domain parameters allowed attackers to bypass authentication checks and escalate privileges.
The patch consolidates test cases and enforces consistent error handling by strictly validating the presence of required parameters during JWT decoding.
The vulnerability is triggered during the JWT token validation process when processing the JWKS URL parameter.
An attacker supplies a crafted JWKS URL containing userinfo or path anomalies to bypass host checks.
The validation logic failed to properly sanitize URLs with userinfo or malformed paths, allowing redirection to untrusted servers.
The patch removes bypass vectors and configures explicit trusted domain properties to prevent unauthorized host redirection.
The vulnerability manifests during the validation of bearer tokens used to authenticate API requests.
Token generation previously omitted tenant identifiers, allowing requests to bypass domain-specific access controls.
The security library failed to strictly enforce tenant and domain binding during token processing, enabling unauthorized privilege escalation.
The patch modifies token creation to explicitly include tenant parameters, ensuring proper isolation and access control enforcement.
The vulnerability manifests during the validation of JSON Web Tokens using OAuth2 service configurations.
The application relies on external OAuth2 service configurations to establish trust and validate incoming tokens.
The validation mechanism fails to strictly verify the UAA domain or service URL, enabling privilege escalation.
The patch replaces direct configuration usage with a mocked instance to explicitly control and verify the UAA domain property during validation.
The vulnerability is triggered during the token verification process where external key retrieval mechanisms are invoked.
The system previously accepted a key set URL directly from the token header without strict validation against the expected service domain.
Relying on an attacker-controlled external URL for cryptographic key retrieval allows bypassing authentication checks, leading to unauthorized privilege escalation.
The patch removes the external URL parameter and associated validation logic, replacing it with an internally constructed URL derived from trusted domain identifiers.
The method serves as the primary entry point for processing incoming HTTP requests and directing them to appropriate response generators.
The system accepts and processes incoming network requests without requiring prior authentication, exposing internal routing logic to external actors.
The routing logic relies on basic string matching for endpoint paths, which fails to properly validate tenant context or restrict access, enabling privilege escalation.
The patch modifies path comparison logic to explicitly account for query parameters and adjusts substring checks to ensure precise request routing and access control.
The vulnerability originates in the service configuration method that constructs authentication domain parameters for OAuth2 services.
The system previously utilized a hardcoded default domain value without incorporating dynamic network port information.
The absence of port handling in the domain string construction resulted in incorrect service endpoint resolution.
The patch introduces conditional port path generation and appends it to the base domain to ensure accurate endpoint targeting.
The function retrieves the public key required to verify JWT signatures, serving as a critical authentication component.
The vulnerability requires processing a JWT that contains a dynamically supplied URI parameter for locating the public key.
The implementation previously accepted a user-supplied URI from the token header without enforcing a secure scheme or validating the domain, enabling potential key substitution.
The patch replaces the token-supplied URI with a configuration-defined domain, appends a tenant identifier parameter, and enforces an absolute HTTPS scheme to prevent unauthorized key retrieval.
The vulnerability is triggered when the application dynamically instantiates socket factory classes based on user-supplied connection properties.
Users can provide arbitrary class names via connection properties, which are directly passed to an object factory for instantiation without prior validation.
The object factory creates instances from the provided class name without verifying that the resulting object matches the expected socket factory type, relying on unsafe casting.
The patch updates the instantiation calls to explicitly pass the expected class type, ensuring the factory validates that the instantiated class conforms to the required interface.
The method dynamically loads a hostname verifier class to validate SSL connections based on user-provided configuration.
The application retrieves a hostname verifier class name from connection properties and passes it to a dynamic instantiation routine.
The object factory instantiates classes from a string name without verifying the resulting object type, allowing unsafe casting to the expected interface.
The patch updates the instantiation call to explicitly specify the expected class type, ensuring the factory validates the object type before assignment.
The application retrieves a class name from user-supplied configuration properties and passes it directly to an object factory for instantiation.
An attacker can supply an arbitrary class name via a configuration property, which the application uses without prior validation.
The object factory instantiates the provided class name without verifying that the resulting object matches the expected interface, enabling arbitrary class instantiation.
The patch modifies the instantiation call to explicitly require the target class to implement the expected interface, preventing arbitrary class loading.
The method serves as the primary entry point for creating instances based on a provided class identifier string.
The system accepts an arbitrary class name and utilizes reflection to dynamically load the corresponding class without verification.
The factory logic fails to verify that the dynamically loaded class conforms to a predefined expected type before instantiation.
The update introduces an expected type parameter and applies a compatibility check to ensure the loaded class matches the required type.
Handles user-submitted approval actions for build promotion via web requests.
The affected endpoint processes promotion requests without enforcing a specific HTTP method, allowing any request type to trigger the action.
The absence of a POST requirement enables cross-site request forgery attacks by allowing attackers to trigger promotions via alternative request methods.
The patch adds a POST annotation to restrict the endpoint to POST requests only, mitigating CSRF risks by ensuring only intentional form submissions trigger promotion.
Handles HTTP requests to schedule and promote builds based on submitted form data.
The affected plugin version allows promotion endpoints to process requests without enforcing a specific HTTP method, making them accessible via GET.
The endpoint fails to validate the HTTP request method, enabling attackers to craft malicious cross-site requests that trigger build promotions without user consent.
The patch adds an HTTP method restriction annotation to the endpoint, ensuring that only POST requests are accepted and mitigating CSRF risks.
The vulnerability affects HTTP endpoints responsible for regular, forced, and re-executed promotions.
The plugin versions prior to 3.9.1 do not enforce POST request methods for promotion actions.
HTTP endpoints implementing promotion fail to require POST requests, enabling cross-site request forgery attacks.
The patch disables the test method to accommodate updated security validation that enforces POST request requirements for promotion endpoints.
This HTTP endpoint handles build promotion requests but lacks method validation.
The plugin version prior to 3.9.1 does not restrict the HTTP method for promotion endpoints, allowing alternative methods to trigger actions.
The absence of a POST request requirement enables cross-site request forgery attacks to force promotions without user consent.
The patch applies the @RequirePOST annotation to the method, ensuring only POST requests are processed and blocking CSRF exploitation.
The vulnerability occurs when custom property values and build display names are processed and rendered on the plugin's web interface.
Attackers must be able to set or change property values and build display names that are subsequently displayed without sanitization.
The plugin fails to escape property values and build display names before rendering them on the Custom Build Properties and Build Summary pages.
The patch refactors the table instantiation to use a parameterized constructor, aligning with the updated logic to properly escape values during rendering.
The method iterates over raw column names, row identifiers, and cell data to populate table structures without prior validation.
The vulnerability requires an attacker to have the ability to set or modify property values and build display names within the application.
Raw values are directly assigned to UI components without neutralizing special characters, enabling stored cross-site scripting attacks.
The patch wraps all raw values with a sanitization function before assignment to prevent malicious content from being rendered.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

nodes.details: This method iterates over buffered JSON properties to deserialize and set values on a target bean during unwrapped property handling.
The deserialization context is configured with a restrictive active view, while the target property is annotated with a broader or different view constraint.
The property iteration loop fails to verify whether the current property is accessible under the active deserialization view before invoking its setter method.
The patch introduces a conditional check that skips property deserialization if an active view is defined and the property is not visible within that view.
The vulnerability occurs during the deserialization of beans using property-based creators, where JSON properties are matched and deserialized into bean fields.
The vulnerability requires a setterless collection or map property that returns true for the merging check, routing it through the regular property buffering path.
The regular property buffering branch lacked a visibility check against the active JSON view, allowing restricted properties to be populated from untrusted input.
The patch adds a visibility check for regular properties against the active view before buffering, ensuring view restrictions are consistently applied to all property types.
The vulnerability is triggered during the initialization of the Konnektor connection factory, where the underlying TLS configuration is established.
An adversary positioned on the communication path between the service and the Konnektor can intercept and manipulate the traffic.
The connection factory is configured to unconditionally accept any server certificate without performing standard validation checks.
The patch replaces the unconditional trust-all configuration with a mechanism to load environment-specific trust managers for proper verification.
The vulnerability originates in the client connection builder, which configures TLS parameters for establishing network communication.
The software is configured to skip standard TLS server certificate verification during the connection initialization phase.
The connection factory accepts any server certificate without validation, allowing attackers to intercept encrypted traffic.
The update replaces the unconditional trust directive with a dedicated trust manager to explicitly control certificate validation behavior.
The module handles cryptographic key loading and initialization, acting as the primary interface for secure communication setup.
An adversary positioned along the communication channel can intercept and manipulate network traffic.
The implementation lacks robust verification mechanisms for presented certificates, enabling substitution with untrusted alternatives.
The update improves diagnostic output by appending the resolved file path to error messages during initialization failures.
The vulnerability occurs during the initialization phase of the network connection's TLS settings.
The connection setup process fails to validate the server certificate against expected domain names.
The underlying configuration constructor is invoked without a parameter to enforce strict certificate subject validation.
The patch updates the configuration initialization to include a default subject alternative name parameter, ensuring proper certificate verification.
The vulnerability is triggered during the creation of the authentication client used for challenge response, where TLS certificate validation is bypassed.
An attacker positioned on the network path between the service and the proxy can intercept traffic. The client initially relies on a default SSL context without custom trust store validation.
The authentication client is instantiated without a custom trust store or discovery validator, allowing acceptance of any TLS certificate including self-signed or expired ones.
The patch introduces a dedicated trust store parameter and wraps the authentication client with a discovery validator to enforce proper certificate validation during the TLS handshake.
The vulnerability occurs during the handling of OpenID Connect discovery responses containing JWT payloads.
An attacker positioned on the network path can intercept responses and present untrusted certificates or modified payloads.
The client extracts and processes the JWT payload without verifying its cryptographic signature or validating the issuer.
The patch adds a validation step to verify the signed JWT before extracting its payload, ensuring trust in the discovery document.
This method initializes the transport layer security parameters for outgoing client connections, directly controlling how server certificates are validated.
The client explicitly bypasses standard certificate common name verification during initialization, creating a state where any presented certificate is accepted.
The configuration disables common name checks without implementing an alternative hostname verification mechanism, allowing man-in-the-middle attacks with arbitrary certificates.
The patch removes the blanket validation bypass and conditionally applies a dedicated hostname verifier based on configured subject alternative names to restore proper identity checks.
The vulnerability targets the plugin's configuration interface, which is accessible via a specific HTTP endpoint.
An attacker with only Overall/Read permissions can reach the configuration interface due to insufficient access controls.
The HTTP endpoint handling plugin configuration lacks necessary permission verification, allowing unauthorized modifications.
The update ensures the configuration endpoint strictly requires Overall/Administer permissions, returning a forbidden status for lower-privilege requests.
The method processes HTTP POST requests to update plugin configuration settings.
The endpoint accepts configuration submissions without verifying the requester's administrative privileges.
The original implementation only enforced POST request validation but failed to implement any role-based access control for the configuration action.
The update adds an explicit administrative permission verification step before processing the configuration data to restrict access.
The method serves as the execution point for a post-launch step that configures and runs a publisher component.
The plugin configuration permits disabling SSL/TLS and hostname verification globally for the Jenkins master JVM.
The publisher initialization omitted a configuration flag to manage certificate validation, causing verification to be disabled.
The patch introduces a new constructor argument to pass the SSL error ignore setting, enabling proper validation control.
The plugin initializes secure connections by invoking a certificate validation bypass routine when fetching remote URLs.
The vulnerability is triggered when the plugin executes remote URL fetching without checking configuration flags before applying the bypass.
The implementation uses static JVM-wide setter methods to disable SSL/TLS and hostname verification, affecting all network connections.
The patch replaces global JVM settings with a dedicated HTTP client instance, restricting the bypass to specific requests based on configuration.
The method configures deserialization behavior for individual properties based on runtime annotations and context.
The issue occurs when a property simultaneously enables case-insensitive matching and applies dynamic property exclusions.
The implementation reconstructs the property collection from the original unfiltered instance rather than the updated contextual instance, effectively discarding prior exclusions.
The patch modifies the reconstruction logic to derive the property collection from the already-modified contextual instance, preserving applied filters.
The vulnerability occurs during the collection of system and JVM information for the Jenkins support bundle, specifically when processing JVM startup arguments.
The support bundle generation process iterates over JVM input arguments and appends them to the output without applying sensitive data redaction.
Sensitive information contained within JVM startup parameters is exposed in the generated support bundle because the code lacks a mechanism to filter or redact passwords and secrets.
The patch introduces a redaction step that processes each JVM argument through a password redactor before appending it to the support bundle output.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Removal of Information Before Storage or Disclosure

nodes.details: The method iterates over agent directory files and adds them to the support bundle container.
The plugin processes agent launch logs without filtering or masking sensitive data before inclusion in the support bundle.
The original implementation directly adds log files to the support bundle without applying keyword-based redaction mechanisms.
The patch replaces the generic file content class with a specialized launch logs handler to enable proper redaction of sensitive keywords.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Removal of Sensitive Information Before Storage

nodes.details: The method processes XML configuration files to identify and mask sensitive data prior to support bundle generation.
The issue occurs when running plugin versions prior to the patch, where support bundle generation fails to capture all sensitive configuration values.
The original detection logic only verifies specific cryptographic patterns, overlooking other sensitive keywords and associated values that require masking.
The patch integrates a dedicated redaction utility to match predefined sensitive keywords and implements state tracking for string elements to ensure comprehensive masking.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Removal of Information Before Storage or Distribution

nodes.details: The vulnerability is triggered when the plugin generates a support bundle containing system and node environment variables.
The issue manifests during the creation of a support bundle that collects environment variables from the controller and connected nodes.
Environment variables are directly written to the support bundle output without filtering or masking sensitive credential values.
The patch intercepts environment variable collection and passes the data through a redaction mechanism before writing it to the output stream.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Removal of Sensitive Information Before Storage or Transmission

nodes.details: The method is responsible for collecting system properties and writing them to the support bundle output stream.
Generating a support bundle in affected plugin versions directly exports system properties without filtering sensitive data.
The implementation directly stores retrieved system properties into the output stream without applying any filtering logic for sensitive keywords.
The patch introduces a redaction step that filters system property values against a keyword list before writing them to the bundle.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Removal of Information Before Storage or Transfer

nodes.details: The method processes and writes file contents to the output stream during support bundle generation.
The vulnerability occurs when the plugin generates a support bundle containing file contents that require sensitive data redaction.
The file content processing pipeline directly passes lines to the content filter without applying a dedicated secrets redaction function, leaving sensitive keywords unmasked.
The patch introduces a secrets filtering function that processes each line before passing it to the content filter, ensuring sensitive values are redacted.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Removal of Information Before Storage or Distribution

nodes.details: This method serves as the entry point for writing file data into the generated support bundle output stream.
The issue occurs when the plugin compiles a support archive that includes files containing confidential or sensitive data.
The original implementation directly streams file contents to the output without filtering or masking sensitive information prior to distribution.
The patch introduces a check against a predefined list of sensitive files, routing them through a redaction process before writing to the output stream.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Removal of Information Before Storage or Distribution

nodes.details: This function processes user-supplied directory and file name parameters to read local log files.
The vulnerability applies when the system is configured to store log files locally, granting direct file system access.
The implementation directly concatenates user-controlled file names with a base directory without validating the resulting path, allowing directory traversal.
The patch normalizes the constructed path and verifies it remains within the intended prefix directory before proceeding with file access.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

nodes.details: The vulnerability is triggered through the log file retrieval interface, as demonstrated by the test assertions targeting file path inputs.
The system must be configured to store log files locally, which enables the path traversal mechanism to access unintended files.
The application processes user-supplied file paths without adequate sanitization, allowing directory traversal sequences to bypass security controls.
The update introduces validation logic to reject malicious path inputs, ensuring the API returns appropriate error codes for unauthorized access attempts.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

nodes.details: An HTTP endpoint designed to populate credential selection lists for job configurations.
The endpoint processes requests from users with only basic read permissions without verifying their authorization level.
The function directly queries the credential store and returns matching identifiers without checking if the requester holds administrative or item-specific privileges.
The patch adds explicit checks for administrative and item-level permissions, returning restricted results if the requester lacks required privileges.
Exposes a web interface for validating FTP server connectivity using provided credentials.
Attackers possessing only read-level permissions can access the functionality without proper authorization.
The endpoint failed to enforce adequate permission checks and request validation before processing credentials.
The patch applies a request method restriction annotation to block unauthorized access attempts.
Serves as the HTTP endpoint for validating FTP server connectivity using provided credentials.
Attackers possessing only Overall/Read permissions can reach the endpoint without elevated privileges.
The method fails to validate user permissions before processing FTP connection parameters, enabling unauthorized credential testing.
The patch adds an administrative permission verification and restricts the endpoint to POST requests to prevent unauthorized access.
This web-accessible method allows users to validate FTP server connectivity using provided credentials through a Jenkins plugin interface.
The endpoint lacks authorization verification, permitting users with only basic read permissions to trigger credential validation routines.
The method executes connection tests with attacker-supplied credentials without verifying administrative or configuration privileges, enabling unauthorized network access attempts.
The patch introduces explicit permission validation requiring administrative or configuration rights based on the request context, and restricts access to POST requests only.
The method processes user-supplied URLs via query parameters to test connectivity, serving as the initial attack surface.
The endpoint accepts requests without requiring a specific HTTP method or verifying the request origin, allowing external actors to trigger it.
The implementation fails to validate request authenticity or enforce administrative privileges before executing server-side requests with user-controlled parameters.
The patch adds a POST requirement annotation and verifies administrative permissions to block unauthorized cross-site requests and restrict access.
The function serves as the entry point for processing user-submitted parameters to test external service connectivity.
The endpoint accepted incoming requests without enforcing specific HTTP methods or anti-CSRF mechanisms, enabling cross-site exploitation.
The logic executed sensitive credential processing without validating whether the requester held required administrative or configuration privileges.
The patch introduces explicit privilege verification for system administration or item configuration before allowing the validation routine to proceed.
The vulnerability is triggered during client connection setup and redirection flows where session state tracking mechanisms are processed before the connection is fully established.

A server can dynamically change the character_set_client variable mid-session through session-state-tracking mechanisms, such as SET NAMES commands executed by stored routines, triggers, or configuration changes.
The driver unconditionally encodes and decodes all character data assuming UTF-8, failing to detect or reject server-initiated charset changes that occur after the initial connection handshake.

The patch introduces an explicit initialization flag during the connection flow and enhances error handling to properly propagate charset-related exceptions, ensuring subsequent non-UTF-8 charset changes are rejected after initialization.
The vulnerability manifests during the reactive connection setup process where session variables and character sets are negotiated with the database server.
A server can dynamically alter the client character set mid-session through configuration or external triggers, which the driver fails to properly intercept.
The driver unconditionally assumes UTF-8 encoding for all data exchange without verifying server-announced charset changes, leading to silent data corruption and potential SQL injection.
The update introduces a connection state tracking mechanism to mark initialization completion, enabling the driver to reject subsequent non-UTF-8 charset changes and close the connection safely.
The vulnerability is triggered when the print feature processes a user-supplied GML layer URL containing external XML references.
An attacker must host a malicious script and DTD file, then supply the external URL as the GML layer address in a print request.
The application parses the remote GML content without disabling external entity resolution, allowing arbitrary file paths to be injected and expanded.
The modification replaces a lengthy inline constructor call with a dedicated helper method. This change encapsulates configuration value initialization to improve test maintainability.
The vulnerability is triggered when the application fetches and parses XML data from user-supplied URLs, specifically within the GML layer handling functionality.
An attacker must host a crafted DTD and script on an external server, and the application must be configured to fetch and process the provided URL as XML input.
The underlying XML parser lacks a custom entity resolver, allowing external entity references to resolve arbitrary local file paths or internal network addresses during parsing.
The patch configures the parser with a custom entity resolver that returns empty input sources for all external entity requests, effectively neutralizing XML external entity attacks.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

nodes.details: The vulnerability originates in the file path resolution logic used by the export procedures to determine target file locations.
Exploitation requires an authenticated user to execute an arbitrary query with the export procedure allowlisted and local file access enabled.
The path validation logic fails to properly resolve directory traversal sequences, allowing malicious paths to escape the expected directory.
The patch normalizes the input URI and replaces real path resolution with canonical file resolution to correctly validate directory traversal sequences.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

nodes.details: The vulnerability is triggered through database queries invoking export procedures that handle file system operations.
Exploitation requires the file export configuration to be enabled, the procedure to be allow-listed, and an attacker to have query execution access.
The export procedures fail to properly sanitize file paths, allowing traversal sequences to write outside the intended directory.
The patch refactors security tests to explicitly assert that illegal file path access throws the expected exception, ensuring robust verification of the directory restriction fix.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

nodes.details: This method processes user-supplied XML definitions to update view configurations, serving as the direct execution path for the vulnerability.
Users with view configuration permissions can submit crafted XML definitions that are subsequently parsed by the application.
The XML transformer factory is instantiated without enabling secure processing features or restricting external resource access, allowing external entity resolution.
The patch configures the transformer factory to enforce secure processing and explicitly disables access to external DTDs and stylesheets to block XXE attacks.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

nodes.details: The vulnerability is triggered during X.509 certificate-based authentication requests processed by the Spring WS security component.
Remote SOAP clients must present X.509 certificates for authentication, causing the provider to evaluate user account status through Spring Security integration.
The authentication provider directly propagates specific Spring Security account status exceptions to remote clients, exposing detailed lifecycle states like disabled or locked accounts.
The patch replaces specific account status exceptions with a generic authentication failure response to prevent remote attackers from inferring account lifecycle states from authentication failures.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

nodes.details: The vulnerability affects integration paths between Spring Web Services and Spring Security that process SOAP messages and handle authentication callbacks.
The system must utilize Spring Web Services integrated with Spring Security to authenticate incoming SOAP requests containing user credentials.

The authentication callback or exception handling logic incorrectly reveals detailed account lifecycle states, such as locked or disabled statuses, instead of returning generic authentication failure messages.
The patch eliminates mock object lifecycle management and verification steps while standardizing test method naming conventions to improve test suite maintainability.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

The utility function proceeds to create a temporary directory without verifying its prior existence.
Failure to verify directory existence before creation results in directories being generated with insecure permissions.
The patch modifies the utility function parameters to align with a corrected implementation that ensures secure directory generation.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere

nodes.details: The utility function serves as the primary interface for generating temporary storage locations within the application.
The creation routine is invoked without first validating whether the target temporary directory already exists on the filesystem.
The implementation proceeds directly to directory creation without checking for pre-existing paths, leading to insecure permission assignment.
The patch modifies the directory instantiation call to enforce proper path handling and prevent insecure permission defaults.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere

nodes.details: The test case invokes this utility method to generate a temporary directory for subsequent file operations.
The application attempts to generate a temporary directory using a utility function without verifying prior existence.
The utility function fails to verify whether the target temporary directory already exists before initiating creation, leading to insecure permissions.
The patch modifies the function invocation to properly handle the returned file object, ensuring correct directory creation and permission handling.

nodes.details: The test method invokes the utility function to allocate a temporary directory for subsequent file processing operations.
The utility function proceeds to create a temporary directory without first verifying whether the target path already exists.
Failure to validate directory existence prior to creation results in the temporary directory being generated with insecure permissions.
The patch eliminates the extension argument from the directory creation invocation to utilize a corrected implementation that properly manages existence checks and permissions.

nodes.details: The test method invokes the utility function responsible for generating temporary directories during execution.
The utility function proceeds to create a temporary directory without first verifying whether the directory already exists in the filesystem.
The absence of an existence check allows concurrent or malicious processes to exploit the directory creation process, leading to insecure permissions.
The patch modifies the function call to utilize an updated implementation that properly handles directory existence and permissions during creation.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere

nodes.details: The utility function is directly invoked to allocate temporary storage for file operations.
The system attempts to generate temporary directories for intermediate file processing without prior validation.
The underlying function does not check for pre-existing directories before creation, resulting in insecure permissions.
The patch modifies function invocations to use a single argument, eliminating redundant suffixes to comply with updated directory creation logic.

nodes.details: The vulnerability originates in the utility function responsible for allocating temporary directories prior to file operations.
The creation routine proceeds without validating whether the target directory path already exists on the filesystem.
Skipping the existence check allows the system to generate directories with overly permissive access controls, enabling unauthorized access.
The patch replaces legacy file object instantiation with a standardized path resolution mechanism to align with updated utility signatures.

nodes.CWE_ID_NAME: Exposure of Resource Number to Unauthorized Control

nodes.details: The vulnerability originates in the temporary directory creation utility function that handles prefix and suffix parameters to generate directory paths.
The application invokes the utility function to allocate temporary directories in the default system temporary location using user-supplied naming parameters.

The implementation generates a temporary file, deletes it, and immediately creates a directory with the identical name without verifying its prior existence, exposing the resource to insecure permissions.
The patch marks the original method as deprecated and delegates execution to a revised single-argument function that eliminates the insecure file-then-delete sequence.
